metadata.scope: Pilot paired comparison; design evaluation only, not broad certification.
metadata.timing_note: Start sampled by date at first reference-read command; finish sampled immediately before response serialization.
metadata.command_count_definition: Nested exec_command invocations in this evaluator, including this final artifact creation and structural validation command; not shell simple-command count.
metadata.token_measurement_note: No session tokenizer/accounting was available. Some tool outputs were truncated, including an overly broad initial file listing; reported per-command original-token estimates do not measure delivered context.
metadata.evidence_path_convention: Case evidence paths are relative to baseline_root and identify actually read files or excerpts, not an assertion that every line was consumed. Glob searches do not imply all matching-file content was read.
observed_gaps: Most extracted method entries retain signatures and one-line summaries rather than full method contracts; CastOptions field semantics, dictionary decode types and selected zero-column behavior were unresolved from these extracts.

The expressions topic says helper construction applies coercion, while the shipped expr_api example separately applies coercion and demonstrates evaluation failure without it. The example informed the narrower responses.
The Parquet reader extract identifies row-group and row-selection APIs but omits their coordinate interaction. E12B explicitly labels its answer as an unverified inference.
No measured optimization break-even or deployment memory guarantee was available; these were not inferred from API availability.

cases.decision: Use the batch filtering kernel; prepare a reusable predicate only for reuse.
cases.decisive_conditions: Mask length must equal batch row count. TRUE selects; FALSE and NULL do not.
cases.contract: Selected rows remain in input order, including duplicates and column nulls. Output keeps column types and schema metadata; no new nulls are introduced. Propagate Arrow errors.
unknowns: The extracted batch method documentation does not spell out length-error behavior or the zero-column implementation.

cases.decision: Use checked take_arrays plus explicit batch construction when bounds control and nullable output are required; take_record_batch is the convenience alternative.
cases.decisive_conditions: Use integer indices; validate non-null indices. Nullable indices require nullable output fields even if source fields were non-nullable.
cases.contract: Output positions are source rows 2,0,2,then an all-null row. Preserve duplicates, requested order, types and metadata. check_bounds=true converts out-of-range indices into errors; unchecked access may panic.
unknowns: Batch convenience API exposes no bounds option; its selected policy and nullable-schema handling are not documented here. Null-index behavior is an inference to verify.
cases.rust_sketch: let cols = take_arrays(batch.columns(), &idx, Some(TakeOptions { check_bounds: true }))?; let out = RecordBatch::try_new(nullable_schema, cols)?;

cases.decision: Prepare one FilterPredicate and reuse it across the 20 arrays; consider optimize before build.
cases.decisive_conditions: Same mask and length for all arrays. Repeated use amortizes mask preparation; selectivity, contiguous runs, array types and size determine benefit.
cases.contract: Each result contains TRUE-mask rows in original order; NULL-mask rows are omitted. Output types and selected value validity survive. Reuse prepared state while processing all arrays.
unknowns: No benchmark or break-even threshold is present in the read evidence.
cases.rust_sketch: let p = FilterBuilder::new(&mask).optimize().build(); let out = arrays.iter().map(|a| p.filter(a.as_ref())).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;

cases.decision: Use direct filter for one small primitive array. The reusable preparation API exists but adds little value without reuse.
cases.decisive_conditions: Mask length matches array length. Direct filter already selects an optimization strategy; manual optimization needs evidence of a benefit.
cases.contract: TRUE selects; FALSE/NULL omit. Stable row order and value nulls remain. Returns the same array type or an Arrow error.
unknowns: One small array does not establish a universal performance threshold; measure if this is a hot path.
cases.rust_sketch: let out = arrow_select::filter::filter(&values, &mask)?;

cases.decision: Use take_record_batch for the two valid non-null indices.
cases.decisive_conditions: The input has two arrays of length three matching schema field count and types. Indices 2 and 0 are in bounds.
cases.contract: Output has two columns and two rows ordered [row2,row0], with the original schema and selected nulls. Ordinary batch construction checks equal lengths and matching data types.
unknowns: The batch take implementation and its bounds-check default were not available in the extracted prose.
cases.rust_sketch: let idx = UInt32Array::from(vec![2, 0]); let out = take_record_batch(&batch, &idx)?;

cases.decision: Validate indices against batch.num_rows(), then explicitly construct a zero-column batch with row_count=2.
cases.decisive_conditions: There is no array length from which construction can infer output row count. The input itself must retain its three-row count.
cases.contract: Preserve the empty schema and its metadata. Output has zero columns and two rows. Bounds must be checked against the batch even though no column kernel runs.
unknowns: The baseline does not show whether take_record_batch internally preserves zero-column row counts; the explicit construction avoids relying on it.

cases.decision: Call cast_with_options with safe=true explicitly.
cases.decisive_conditions: Input is Utf8 strings with a malformed numeric value; result type is Int32. Safe parsing should replace malformed entries with null.
cases.contract: Expected result is [Some(12),None,None], same length/order. Existing null remains null. Unsupported type conversions can still error; this is not universal error suppression. Rebuild any batch field as nullable Int32.
unknowns: Field-level safe documentation and its default were omitted; the option interpretation needs an executable check.
cases.rust_sketch: let options = CastOptions { safe: true, ..Default::default() }; let out = cast_with_options(&strings, &DataType::Int32, &options)?;

cases.decision: Call cast_with_options with safe=false explicitly and propagate failure.
cases.decisive_conditions: Strict parsing must reject "bad" rather than turn it into a null.
cases.contract: Expected result is Err(ArrowError) for the supplied input; no successful partial array. A valid nullable input would preserve nulls and order while producing Int32. Do not convert the whole error into a null array.
unknowns: Extracted CastOptions lists field names but omits their definitions; exact error variant/message and safe behavior remain unverified.
cases.rust_sketch: let options = CastOptions { safe: false, ..Default::default() }; let out = cast_with_options(&strings, &DataType::Int32, &options)?;

cases.decision: Encode composite keys with one RowConverter configured with per-column sort options.
cases.decisive_conditions: Use the same converter for all rows being compared; column types and lengths match its fields. Set descending and nulls_first separately per key.
cases.contract: Row comparison follows the encoded lexicographic ordering. Borrowed Row lifetime follows Rows; owned() detaches a single row. Retain converter configuration and storage. Float ordering is total and can distinguish signed zero.
unknowns: Unsupported types must be checked with supports_fields or construction errors. No runtime compatibility probe was run.

cases.decision: Persist typed Arrow batches with IPC and a versioned comparison-policy description; regenerate row keys after loading.
cases.decisive_conditions: Durability spans processes and upgrades. RowConverter encoding may change between releases and comparisons require the same converter.
cases.contract: Preserve schema, values, nulls and column order in IPC; store sort directions/null placement separately. Finish the writer before publication, validate read schema, and construct one local converter on read. Do not persist raw Rows bytes as stable keys.
unknowns: Long-term compatibility across specific producer/consumer releases needs separate round-trip tests and a migration policy.

cases.decision: Compare hydrated logical values. For an explicit decode type, cast dictionary string columns to Utf8 before row conversion.
cases.decisive_conditions: Only logical values matter; physical dictionary key types, unused entries and assignments may be discarded.
cases.contract: Use Utf8 SortFields for hydrated strings. convert_rows on this converter yields Utf8 arrays, preserving values/nulls and selected row order, not Dictionary<K,Utf8>. Composite comparisons use one converter.
unknowns: Direct dictionary-input convert_rows decoded physical types are not stated in the baseline; explicit hydration avoids depending on that missing contract.

cases.decision: Use row encoding only for comparison, retaining original dictionary arrays and row identities as a sidecar.
cases.decisive_conditions: Exact dictionary physical types and key assignments cannot be recovered from a representation that hydrates only logical values.
cases.contract: Reconstruct Dictionary<K,V> from gathered original PrimitiveArray<K> keys and the unchanged values array. Preserve null keys, unused dictionary entries and original assignments. Row-decoded comparison values alone are insufficient; retain sidecar until reconstruction completes.
unknowns: The direct convert_rows dictionary output contract is missing; no exact physical round-trip claim is made for it.

cases.decision: Use execute_stream and await each consumer operation. Use partitioned streams only when partition-aware consumption is useful.
cases.decisive_conditions: Avoid retaining batches or unbounded consumer queues. collect materializes all result batches.
cases.contract: Streaming bounds consumer retention to currently processed batches, not query-wide memory. Blocking operators may buffer extensively. Results and errors arrive incrementally; schema follows the plan. No global order without an ordering requirement. Drop stream on cancellation.
unknowns: No measured peak memory or cancellation cleanup evidence is available.

cases.decision: Stream output and configure a limited memory pool plus bounded temporary spill storage before creating the session.
cases.decisive_conditions: A blocking sort buffers/spills before yielding. Limit target partitions and consumer queues; reserve memory for untracked batches and overhead.
cases.contract: Pool budget constrains tracked operator reservations, not process RSS. Spill-capable operators spill or fail; disk exhaustion can fail. Require physical-plan inspection, spill metrics, pool peak and RSS measurements under representative large input before guaranteeing a deployment budget.
unknowns: Sort completion, spill behavior, cleanup and peak RSS were not tested; an OS/container limit would be needed for a hard process bound.

cases.contract: Register the Arc provider and query it normally. Batches remain materialized in memory; registration does not establish a memory budget or global row ordering. Preserve duplicates/nulls; reject incompatible batch construction. Custom providers remain an option for special execution/source semantics.
unknowns: Exact schema-compatibility acceptance details and empty-partition handling are not shown in the extracted constructor documentation.

cases.decision: Use registered object storage with Parquet registration/ListingTable. A custom provider is unnecessary unless custom indexes or source behavior are required.
cases.decisive_conditions: Declare partition columns, register the object store URL and configure Parquet pruning. Metadata/statistics must exist for effective pruning.
cases.contract: Built-ins discover files, add partition columns, manage schema inference/adaptation and apply projection/filter pushdown. Missing compatible columns may become null. No global order follows from file discovery. Inspect EXPLAIN ANALYZE and I/O/pruning metrics; eligibility is not proof of actual skipped data.
unknowns: Object-store authentication, exact feature set and observed pruning are unverified.

cases.decision: Return Exact for each predicate fully implemented with SQL semantics; Unsupported for unsupported predicates.
cases.decisive_conditions: Every TRUE row must survive, every FALSE/NULL row must be removed. Evaluation coverage includes all candidate rows and preserves multiplicities.
cases.contract: Return one classification per input expression in the same order. Exact allows DataFusion to remove the residual filter, making this a correctness contract.
unknowns: No classifier or oracle was executed.
cases.rust_sketch: Ok(filters.iter().map(|f| if supported(f) { Exact } else { Unsupported }).collect())
cases.correctness_oracle: For k=[NULL,1,2,2,3], k>=2 yields [2,2,3]. Compare pushed execution against an unfiltered MemTable plus DataFusion WHERE, as multisets; inspect plan for residual removal.

cases.decision: Return Inexact for supported conservative metadata pruning.
cases.decisive_conditions: Candidate groups must contain every potentially matching row. Unknown/incomplete statistics retain groups; false positives are allowed, false negatives are not.
cases.contract: DataFusion retains a residual filter to enforce SQL TRUE semantics. Preserve duplicate matching rows; metadata cannot justify Exact merely because it is accurate min/max metadata. Limit must not truncate candidates before residual evaluation.
unknowns: No metadata-pruning implementation or runtime oracle was executed.
cases.rust_sketch: Ok(filters.iter().map(|f| if metadata_supports(f) { Inexact } else { Unsupported }).collect())
cases.correctness_oracle: Compare final results to unpruned MemTable WHERE on nulls, duplicates and boundary values. Separately prove candidate multiset contains every matching source row; include groups mixing 1,2,2,NULL for k>=2.

cases.decision: Build a scan execution plan that evaluates supported predicates against the full source schema and filters batches during execution.
cases.decisive_conditions: Assume projection=None because all columns are requested. Advertise Exact only for implemented predicates; combine filters with AND.
cases.contract: scan plans rather than performs heavy work. Execution yields schema-matching batches, selects only TRUE, preserves multiplicity and does not invent ordering guarantees. Propagate expression/read errors. Evaluate before limiting; avoid claiming sorting absent evidence.
unknowns: Concrete source execution-plan plumbing remains application-specific.
cases.correctness_oracle: Compare full output schema and row multiset to unfiltered MemTable WHERE using NULL, duplicate and boundary rows; empty/all-false batches must remain valid.

cases.decision: Read predicate columns internally, filter against the full internal schema, then project requested columns and apply a safe post-filter limit.
cases.decisive_conditions: Projection indices refer to table schema; output must match requested column order/types. A removed predicate column is still required for evaluation. Exact predicates permit early stop after enough matching rows.
cases.contract: FALSE/NULL rows do not count toward the limit. Preserve duplicate matches. Do not apply the limit to pre-filter candidates or before an Inexact residual filter. Coordinate limit handling across partitions or let DataFusion enforce it. Keep planning lightweight.
unknowns: Exact provider limit-hint contract and cross-partition implementation are not detailed in read extracts.
cases.rust_sketch: let kept = filter_record_batch(&batch, &mask)?; let projected = kept.project(projection)?; // emit matching rows up to coordinated limit
cases.correctness_oracle: Compare to SELECT payload FROM oracle WHERE k>=2 LIMIT 2. Include leading NULL/nonmatches and duplicate payloads. Use deterministic ORDER BY or relational limit properties when comparing unordered results.

cases.decision: Let ordinary SQL planning/analyzer perform coercion before optimization and physical evaluation.
cases.decisive_conditions: Registered schema determines operand types. Mixed types need a supported common coercion; incompatible combinations should error.
cases.contract: Expr construction describes computation. Analysis resolves names/types and inserts casts; simplification rewrites constants/algebra with schema/nullability context. Physical expression evaluation produces ColumnarValue/Arrow batches and may still raise data-dependent errors. A helper constructor alone does not prove type compatibility.
unknowns: No concrete operand pair was specified, so exact result type/coercion cannot be promised.

cases.decision: Explicitly coerce against DFSchema before calling the standalone simplifier. Reject operands without a supported coercion.
cases.decisive_conditions: Direct construction and simplify are not substitutes for normal analysis. SessionContext::create_physical_expr supplies coercion; the lower-level function may not.
cases.contract: Build SimplifyContext with the correct schema and execution-time context, coerce, simplify, then create/evaluate the physical expression. Propagate coercion/evaluation errors and preserve SQL null semantics. Simplification returns an Expr, not row results.
unknowns: Exact behavior of simplifying a genuinely incompatible expression was not executed; do not rely on it to reject all invalid trees.

cases.decision: Build selection ranges over the retained file row sequence, which is the whole file when every row group is retained.
cases.decisive_conditions: Coordinates count rows, not bytes or output positions. Use ordered nonoverlapping ranges and the total row count.
cases.contract: Selection produces a subset in file order; it is not arbitrary gather/reordering. with_row_filter evaluates predicates during decoding; source/page pruning can avoid I/O earlier. RowSelection can skip fetches when page metadata supports it but does not itself evaluate SQL predicates. Preserve selected values/nulls and reader schema.
unknowns: Exact malformed-selection errors and I/O savings are unverified.
cases.rust_sketch: let s = RowSelection::from_consecutive_ranges(vec![2..4, 8..9].into_iter(), total_rows); let reader = builder.with_row_selection(s).build()?;

cases.decision: Use row selection coordinates over the concatenated retained row groups; omit excluded groups from selection offsets.
cases.decisive_conditions: For three ten-row groups retaining [0,2], original row 22 maps to selection offset 12, not 22. Preserve retained-group traversal order.
cases.contract: Row-group pruning removes whole groups; row selection narrows rows/pages inside the remaining sequence; RowFilter evaluates while decoding. These stages differ from filtering already decoded batches. Output retains selected values/nulls with the reader schema; no arbitrary gather duplication is provided.
unknowns: The extracted with_row_selection method contract omits its interaction with with_row_groups; the coordinate rule is an unverified design inference requiring an integration probe.
